title: Amitabh Bachchan Turns 84: Tributes, Scholarships and a Teary KBC Moment for the Shahenshah
excerpt: The industry poured out tributes for the superstar's 84th — from Sanjay Dutt and Chiranjeevi to a producer's scholarships for 1,000 students — while a recording of his late mother's voice moved the KBC studio.
body:
• Amitabh Bachchan turned 84 on Sunday, October 11, with fans gathering outside his Mumbai residence Jalsa and the industry pouring out tributes.
  • Producer Anand Pandit marked the day with scholarships for 1,000 students through the Lotus Foundation, plus hoardings across Mumbai and birthday greetings on cinema screens nationwide.
  • On Kaun Banega Crorepati, a recording of his late mother Teji Bachchan reciting Harivansh Rai Bachchan's poem brought an emotional moment to the studio.
  • Sanjay Dutt, Chiranjeevi, Kajol and Kamal Haasan were among those who honoured the actor, last seen with Rajinikanth in Vettaiyan and upcoming in Kalki 2898 AD Part 2.

Amitabh Bachchan celebrated his 84th birthday on Sunday, and the day belonged to him as completely as the last five decades have. Fans gathered outside his Mumbai home, Jalsa, singing songs from his films and carrying his photographs. Colleagues from every corner of Indian cinema paid tribute. And on the Kaun Banega Crorepati set, a ghost from his past — his mother Teji Bachchan's voice reciting his father's poem — gave the birthday its most emotional moment.

The tributes

Sanjay Dutt, who has shared the screen with Bachchan in Kaante, Hum Kisise Kum Nahin, Deewaar, Eklavya, Shootout at Lokhandwala and Department, called him "my hero" and credited him as a formative influence on his career. Telugu megastar Chiranjeevi addressed him as his "dearest Guru Ji," writing that Bachchan's warmth and humility make him special beyond his towering achievements. Kajol dubbed him a "witty and uber cool natural phenomenon" on Instagram, alongside a photo from her KBC appearance with him.

Kamal Haasan — who shared the screen with Bachchan in Geraftaar (1985) and Kalki 2898 AD — wrote that Bachchan could make even a simple "Deviyon aur Sajjano" sound like a blockbuster opening, and reminded fans that the two legends will reunite in Kalki 2898 AD Part 2.

"The fire we first witnessed in Zanjeer is still burning bright. Even today, he brings the energy of a newcomer to his work, along with the wisdom and gravitas of a master."

— Producer Anand Pandit

The scholarships

Pandit chose to honour his "friend, idol and guiding light" by looking beyond cinema: in association with the Lotus Foundation, he will provide educational scholarships to 1,000 deserving students, while hoardings across Mumbai and birthday greetings on cinema screens across India carry the celebrations to audiences who have followed Bachchan's journey for generations. It continues a pattern: in 2022, Pandit pledged meals for 8,000 children and 800 hearing aids on Bachchan's 80th birthday, and in 2023 dedicated over 8,100 trees to create the 'Amitabh Bachchan Grove'.

The KBC moment

Ahead of the birthday, the Kaun Banega Crorepati studio played a recording of the late Teji Bachchan reciting her husband Harivansh Rai Bachchan's poem "Raat Aadhi Ho Gayi Hai." Bachchan's visible emotion offered viewers a rare glimpse of the son behind the superstar — a reminder that the man who has played gods and gangsters on screen remains, at 84, a son carrying his parents' words.

Context: a career that invented reinvention

Born October 11, 1942, in Allahabad — now Prayagraj — Bachchan debuted with Saat Hindustani in 1969 and became the "Angry Young Man" of the 1970s, then reinvented himself through the 1980s and 90s, survived a near-death on set and a corporate collapse, and rebuilt himself as television's most trusted face with Kaun Banega Crorepati. More than five decades on, he is still hosting, still acting, and still working. His most recent screen appearance was opposite Rajinikanth in Vettaiyan; the Kalki sequel with Kamal Haasan awaits.

Diaspora angle

For the diaspora, Bachchan is the throughline of Indian popular culture abroad: the voice that introduced India to living rooms from London to New Jersey, the KBC host whose catchphrases cross generations of immigrant families. His birthday is as much a diaspora ritual as an Indian one — observed wherever Hindi cinema has travelled, which is everywhere.

What's next

The actor shows no sign of slowing. Kalki 2898 AD Part 2 will reunite him with Kamal Haasan, and Kaun Banega Crorepati continues to anchor his week. At 84, the Shahenshah still sets the terms.
